# 1 Clement Chapter 4 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic Equivalence)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 4 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_004_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 4

**4:1** Scripture gives us the clearest example: "After some time had passed, Cain brought an offering from the produce of the earth to God. Abel also brought an offering — the firstborn of his flock and their fat portions. God looked with favor on Abel and his offering, but on Cain and his offering he did not look with favor. So Cain became deeply distressed and his face fell." [Gen 4:3-5]

**4:2** "Then God said to Cain, 'Why are you so distressed, and why has your face fallen? If you made your offering rightly but didn't divide it rightly, haven't you sinned? Calm down. Your brother's desire will be toward you, and you will rule over him.'" [Gen 4:6-7]

**4:3** "Cain said to his brother Abel, 'Let's go out into the field.' While they were in the field, Cain attacked his brother Abel and killed him." [Gen 4:8]

**4:4** You see it, brothers? Jealousy and envy produced a fratricide.

**4:5** It was jealousy that made our ancestor Jacob flee from his brother Esau. [Gen 27:41ff]

**4:6** It was jealousy that caused Joseph to be hunted down and sold into slavery. [Gen 37]

**4:7** It was jealousy that forced Moses to run from Pharaoh, king of Egypt, after a fellow Israelite challenged him: "Who made you our ruler and judge? Are you going to kill me the way you killed that Egyptian yesterday?" [Exod 2:14]

**4:8** It was jealousy that got Aaron and Miriam shut out of the camp. [Num 12:14-15]

**4:9** It was jealousy that sent Dathan and Abiram down alive into Hades for rising up against Moses, the servant of God. [Num 16:33]

**4:10** It was jealousy that brought David face-to-face with envy — not only from foreigners, but even from Saul the king of Israel, who actively hunted him. [1 Sam 18:6ff]

---

*PNEUMA dynamic equivalence — Clement's gallery of jealousy's victims rendered for impact.*
